meanings.note: Colloquial. Common masculine noun meaning 'mess, chaos' in everyday Russian.

There was total chaos in the room.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'watch out / beware'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и беречься вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and watch out on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют беречься.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to watch out.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'forever'.
Secondary conversational sense ('constantly, always') (colloquial expression of annoyance) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You're right, one cannot be afraid forever.

meanings.note: Lasting forever. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('eternal, everlasting, perpetual').
Never-ending. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('eternal, everlasting, perpetual').

examples.trans: Nothing lasts forever under the moon.

examples.text: Знаешь, что это за часы? Швейцария! Они вечные.
examples.trans: Do you know what kind of watch this is? Switzerland! It'll last forever.

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact, for the record
meanings.note: Polite or pointed correction. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.

examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'complain'.

examples.text: Да я обязательно буду на вас жаловаться!
examples.trans: I will definitely complain about you!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и жаловаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and complain on time.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: in advance, beforehand, ahead of time
meanings.note: Temporal adverb. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ранее').

examples.trans: Did you set all this up in advance?

examples.text: Мы купили билеты на поезд заранее.
examples.trans: We bought the train tickets in advance.

examples.text: Тогда заранее желаю вам приятного аппетита!
examples.trans: Then in advance I wish you bon appétit!

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Takes the instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'in front of, before' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'in front of, before' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm standing in front of you.
There's a car in front of the house.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Пить чай = to drink tea. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drink', paired with 'выпить'.
used on its own: он пьёт = he drinks

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.en: to warn, to give advance notice
meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упреждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to warn', paired with 'предупредить'.

examples.trans: I am warning you for the last time.

examples.text: О чём предупреждал? Да ты что делаешь?
examples.trans: Warned me about what? Hey, what are you doing?

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Что происходит? = What is going on?

examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: Простите! = sorry! forgive me!. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

Imperative: прости / простите. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прашивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спросить'.

examples.text: Вот это что такое, я вас спрашиваю!
examples.trans: What is this, I'm asking you!
